newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Monday's rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Monday's rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Tuesday after ending mostly higher in a thin lackluster session Monday.
"We're still seeing strength," a West Coast electricity dealer said.

In over-the-counter trade, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $16.70-16.90 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared to Monday's settlement of $16.57, with June Palo Verde (PV) at $22.30-22.70 versus yesterday's close of $22.37.
Market sources said a rebound in next-day physical power prices due to hot weather in parts of Southwest are pulling forward prices higher.

Most of the Southwest is also predicted to see dry and warmer-than-normal spring temperatures through next week. The California coast in the meantime would experience seasonal readings in the high-60s to low-80s.

Next-day power values in the West were also bolstered by news that Bonneville Power Administration will postpone increasing capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission lines until at least mid-week.

The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council approved last Friday raising the Intertie rating to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from 6,250 MW, but the increase was contingent on a transfer capability study, a BPA spokeswoman said.

A warm, dry weather system is expected to stay over the Northwest into next week. Temperatures would run well above normal in the western sections, above normal in the central areas and near normal in the eastern region.
The power complex would likely shrug off weakness in the natural gas market. NYMEX June Henry Hub futures opened down 4.4 cents at $2.180 per million British thermal units.
Trading volume would likely remain light with many players attending various industry functions around the country this week, market sources noted.
